title: Establishing a new alveolar cleft model in rats to investigate the influence of jaw reconstructions on orthodontic tooth movement
authors: Möhlhenrich SC, Heitzer M, Magnuska Z, Gremse F, Chhatwani S, Danesh G, Hölzle F, Modabber A. Ann Anat. 2021 Jul;236:151713. doi: 10.1016/j.aanat.2021.151713.
supports: Pre-clinical study from the botiss maxresorb / maxresorb inject (biphasic CaP) literature list — the product featured in it, which is not the same as the study being about the product, so check the design and the comparator before citing it as product evidence. Authors' conclusion, verbatim: “Surgical interventions in the oral cavity of rats requires a stronger anesthesia and lead to increased risk of coolant and coagulated blood aspiration. The new alveolar cleft model in rats allows for subsequent orthodontic tooth movement after cleft repair, but only in the mesial root of the first molar” This records what the paper says, not what a rep may say: the sales wording still has to pass the claim tiers, and a study in one indication licenses nothing in another.
